_note: Config for python/pick_and_place.py. Distances in mm, robot base frame (X forward, Y left, Z up, origin = base axis at table level). Values marked *_measured=false are estimates; --execute refuses to run until they are measured and set to true.

camera._note_source: source: serial = ESP32-CAM on port, usb = webcam whose name contains usb_name. --camera overrides it.
camera._note_mirror: The ESP32-CAM image is left-right mirrored; true flips it back in SerialCamera.
camera._note_delay: frame_delay_s: how far behind the camera runs. Each look in visual_pick.py skips frames until this long after the arm stopped, so it never aims with a picture taken mid-move. The ESP32-CAM sends each JPEG over serial at 460800 baud (about 0.3-0.5 s); on 2026-11-13 aiming saw the arm's previous position. Raise it if the aim still swings.

table._note: homography maps 640x480 pixels to table-plane XY. Build it with --calibrate-homography.

aruco._note_tray: Stick the tray marker flat at TABLE level (next to the tray) so the homography is valid; offset_xy_mm goes from the marker centre to the drop point.
aruco._note_calib: Marker centres (robot XY, mm) used by --calibrate-homography. Need at least 4, spread over the work area.

arm._note: Link lengths from docs/arm_drawing_reference.png estimates. Zero pose: upper arm and forearm horizontal, pointing +X.
arm._note_wrist: wrist_mode 'vertical' drives wrist pitch so the gripper points straight down. 'fixed' leaves the wrist servo alone (e.g. a 360-degree servo) and solves IK with the wrist held at wrist_fixed_deg.
arm._note_home: Home/standby pose as servo angles shown in servo_control_app.py (base, shoulder, elbow, wrist roll, wrist pitch); same as its Standby button. Disabled joints are not driven.

joints._note: One entry per DDQN joint [base, shoulder, elbow, wrist_pitch, wrist_roll, spare]. servo_deg = center_deg + direction * joint_deg. center_deg = servo angle when the joint is at the zero pose. Disable joints driven by 360-degree servos.

gripper._note_grip: visual_pick.py closes to grip_deg and keeps PWM on until release. 50 matches the Grip button in servo_control_app.py.
gripper._note_close: close_s: seconds to close the jaws gradually, so the first jaw to touch does not flick the object away.
gripper._note_size: Grip angle from the object's width (visual_pick_config objects <name> grip width_mm): the jaws are taken to open evenly with the angle, from jaw_closed_deg (jaws just touching) to open_deg (jaw_open_mm apart), and close squeeze_mm narrower than the object so it is held firmly. jaw_closed_deg and jaw_open_mm measured 2026-11-13. Objects without width_mm use grip_deg.
gripper._note_safe: safe_min_deg: the gripper is never commanded below this. Further closed, an SG90 pushing on a hard object stalls, draws high current and can burn out.
